title: Kent Test day: a calm checklist for parents
description: A simple checklist for the night before and the morning of the Kent Test, from the answer sheet to breakfast, with what to say to your child.
content:
The practical side of test day is easy to forget when you are focused on the content. This checklist draws on the guidance Quest Assessments publishes for families and the council’s information. Use what is helpful and leave the rest.

## Before the day

- **Check the arrangements.** Children at Kent primary schools usually sit the test at their own school. Children at primary schools outside Kent may be invited to sit it at a Kent grammar school the following weekend. Look at the council’s page for the dates.
- **Practise the answer sheet.** Make sure your child has marked a sample sheet with a single line. Anything written in the question booklet is not marked.
- **Talk it through.** Explain that the test is meant to be challenging, that nobody is expected to finish everything, and that the aim is to do their best.

## The night before

- Pack pencils and a good eraser, so the morning is calm. Follow any other instructions you have been given about what to bring.
- Stop practising. A relaxed evening of reading, music or a game is better than a last revision session.
- Aim for an early night.

## The morning

- **A proper breakfast.** Quest suggests a healthy meal and avoiding anything very sugary that could leave a child sluggish later.
- **Allow plenty of time for the journey,** and keep the tone light. Your child will take their lead from you. Say you are proud of the work they have put in.
- **Remind them of three habits:** read each question carefully, check how many answers are needed, and answer every question.

## What your child can do on the day

- Do not talk to anyone except the invigilator while the test is under way, which is Quest’s reminder to families. Listen carefully to the invigilator’s instructions. If they cannot hear, or need to ask something, they should put their hand up.
- Do not spend too long on any one question. If unsure, choose the most likely answer and move on, then return if time allows.
- Use the question booklet for working out, but mark every answer on the answer sheet.
- If nerves arrive, take a slow breath in and out. Nerves mean they care.

## Afterwards

Do something enjoyable together, and let them talk about it, or not, as they wish. Results come later, on a date the council sets. Whatever the outcome, the reading, reasoning and confidence your child has built carry over into every school.

*Sagito is an independent app and is not affiliated with Kent County Council, Quest Assessments or any school. Check dates and arrangements on [Kent County Council’s Kent Test pages](https://www.kent.gov.uk/education-and-children/schools/school-places/kent-test) before you rely on them.*
